APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 5, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:04 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Martinez Muela  4-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.7.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: No
  material submitted.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Roberto Rios – My name is Roberto Rios , I'm a long time Resident and property owner
in the city of El Monte, I came to this city over 50 years ago with my family of 12 Siblings,
7 sisters and 5 Brothers we all went to school here, this city was a very beautiful place
with lots of work low crime mid box stores, Etc. but something went wrong I seen mayors
come and go including our fire department was trade for some votes to be elected for
city mayor, I'm tired of seen our city Appointees not do what they promises, and use the
position for their own gain, I'm glad we finally got rid of mayor Quintero and his partner in
crime Velasco. I'm writing this letter to ask the city council and elected Mayor Jessica to
please make a good decision, and not go with a special election and save the tax payers
$300.000 dollars, we can use the money for some good things for our city, like patching
potholes in residential areas, or fix some sidewalks witch they are potential liability to our
city , I'm a father of a special needs child who gets around on a wheelchair, with this stay
at home order we do more walking around our block, every time we come to this broken
sidewalks we have to go in to the street putting our self in danger. please use the other
option and appoint a city council we have a good Candidate winch could easily fill this
position, her name is Irma Zamorano a long time resident of El Monte a person who
really cares about our city and children, I have seen her all over our city helping in
different events for the benefit of our residents, she's a strong and intelligent woman,
who always has the best interest of our people and not of corporate, I'm endorsing Irma
Zamorano and with this letter I'm casting my vote for her. Thank you.

Kevin Fonseca – The language that the man at First Works Baptist Church is speaking is
hateful, offensive and is sparking fear in people. People and children should not have to
walk around in fear of judgement, harassment or harm because of the hate someone is
speaking and stirring up in our city. Although they have not done any damage or harm
yet, the repercussions and the damage this kind of hatred and evil can have on our city
and its residents is far too great to not take any action. We need to start attracting
people who are going to add to our community, taking care of the residents who live
here and have grown up here for generations and people who are trying to create a
better life for themselves and their families. This institute is the opposite of all those
things and will attract more of this negativity to our communities that we do not need.
This is an issue. It needs to be addressed. It cannot be swept under the rug. It’s not

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

going anywhere, the LGBTQIA community is not going anywhere, but this church needs
to go somewhere other than our city of El Monte.

Julianne Quezada – First Works Baptist Church located at 2600 Tyler Ave. El Monte, CA
91733 does not adhere to Los Angeles County COVID-19 guidelines and the current
stay at home order. As you all know, El Monte has a disproportionate amount of COVID-
19 cases compared to other surrounding cities. This establishment can cause increased
community spread of the virus, which is the exact opposite of what we need. Our
community is filled with essential workers who already are at a higher risk for contracting
the virus. We do not need a place that openly hosts super spreader events that can be
detrimental to the city. The church gathers 3-5 times a week with large crowds, and
there are typically no masks and social distancing. This can be seen on their Instagram
page, which is @fwbc_la, and on their pastor’s Instagram page, @wild_olive_tree. The
lack of masks and social distancing can also be found on their YouTube page, where
they live stream and post their weekly sermons. I will link this YouTube page below for
you to view. Additionally, I will link the Southern Law Poverty Center’s recognition of the
First Works Baptist Church as a hate group, so you can truly see how dangerous their
rhetoric and ideologies are. Their rhetoric about inciting violence on queer people and
the false narrative they perpetuate about queer people is extremely concerning for our
community. They make people in our community feel unsafe, and I don’t believe that is
okay. If you would like, I can provide you supplemental information about this church’s
hateful, vile, and dangerous rhetoric that poses a threat to our city. I am in contact with
organizers in the area who are all in communication about our research of the church.
On Instagram, you can contact @keepelmontefriendly for any needed information or
further action. My phone number is below if you have any other questions or concerns.
Thank you for taking the time to read this. I hope you all consider the voices of your
constituents who have these urgent concerns that need immediate attention.

Dulce Santana – I am here because I am part of the El Monte Community. I have been
part of the El Monte Community for approximately 30 years. Recently I heard word
about a church in El Monte

Stephanie Ramos – I want to know what is going to be done about First Works Baptist
Church in El Monte and the hate speech and discrimination because of the no homo
allowed signs you name it is out there. I saw a comment you saying that you stand in
solidarity with the community but we want to know what are going to be done.

Camila Camaleón –My name is Camila Camaleón and I am the current President of the
San Gabriel Valley LGBTQ+ Center. We are a nonprofit that advocates for people of all
orientations and gender identities. With the spotlight on El Monte recently we send this
statement to your City Council in hopes of it being read at tonight's public comment. We
highlight that our center does not stand for any hate and look forward to any potential
steps we can be involved with. With the above stated, our organization will begin doing
introductions at various City Council's starting February and I'd love to hear how we
could do a brief presentation at El Monte's to discuss the nature of our work. I thank you
for your time and am looking forward to speaking with you all soon.

Ayble Juarez – I am a spokesperson for the Instagram account "Keep El Monte
Friendly". I am a transgender male and I feel my life is being threatened by the First
Works Baptist Church. I would like to thank Mayor Ancona for speaking out and
acknowledging the issue but I do not believe it is enough. Members of this 'church' have
been threatening us. They have been sending death threats and telling me that they

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

want me to burn in hell. We are facing constant harassment and I do not feel safe with
these people in our city. I am asking you to take further action. Thank you.

Cindy Nguyen – As you all may well know, First Works Baptist Church on Tyler Ave.
poses a real threat to not only the LGBTQ+ community but also the working class people
of El Monte. Not only have they been spewing hate online (i.e. telling the f-word to burn
in hell or to die), they have also been congregating without any masks or social
distancing. We are dealing with both a moral and health issue here. If you city officials
truly cared for the El Monte people, act like it and please denounce them as a hate
group. They will only be so much more fueled by hate if nothing were to be ever done to
them. Every one of their actions needs to be met with serious consequences. Also, why
are we waiting for a person to die before taking any action? Hasn't 2020 already shown
us that we have to become a better society and care for another? With that being said,
again, please listen to the individuals who are outraged and who are speaking out
against this man and his 'church'. Thank you.

Cosme Jimenez – I have a question about the expenses for marijuana the $90,000 we
are paying the City Attorney $16,000. I want to know when this is going to stop.

Alyssa Acosta – First Works Baptist Church, located at 2600 Tyler Ave, El Monte, CA
91733, is a ministry led by Bruce Mejia. Mejia twists God's word and actively
discriminates against the LGBTQIA+ community. He also encouraged, to his entire
congregation, that he wants to give more business to a local El Monte barbershop that
hatefully & purposely cut a gay man’s hair up. I am worried that Mejia and members of
his church will enact actions of violence against the many LGBTQ+ people living in or
visiting El Monte. We are asking you to recognize FWBC as a hate group (as Maywood
has) and help take them out of the city. As someone who values El Monte, it's residents,
and is a proud ally of the LGBTQ+ community, I am saddened to see that you are
allowing this type of bigotry to freely exist in the neighborhood, a city I grew up in and
continue to spend time in. We need to let Bruce Mejia and his following know that they
are not welcome here. The city of El Monte and its constituents do not condone this
"church" and want their members to know that they cannot congregate here. In addition
to their hateful ways, they are going against COVID-19 guidelines by having several
households gather indoors with no masks, proven by social media posts that he has
posted. (Videos and photos) Mejia’s personal Instagram is @wild_olive_tree and his
church Instagram is @fwbc_la, just so you’re able to see for yourself. El Monte has
historically been a refuge and should continue to serve as a safe space for all people
regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity. And the people agree, there is a
petition that has gathered over 9,000 signatures and still counting. Let us come together
and show that love trumps hate. In 2021, I hope that we can move forward to spread
love and acceptance to future generations instead of digressing to hateful ways. We
must come together to shut FWBC down.

Samatha Villa – I have lived in El Monte my whole life and it’s a city I loved to be raised
in. A city that I know can have such beautiful community and unity. However, a new
terror has entered El Monte and has brought a toxic environment to stain our beautiful
home. First Works Baptist Church located on Tyler Ave is an immediate threat to the
safety of the people in our city- the people that the City Council is obliged to protect and
voted in to protect. The church’s pastor Bruce Mejia preaches hate, intolerance, anti-
semitism and threatens harm to those who are LGBTQ and who are against his hate
sermons. I’m afraid for those I love and I’m afraid that if we don’t stop them now, they
will only bring violence to Friendly El Monte. Please consider finding a way to expel this
  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

  hate group from our city and by doing so keeping the ‘Friendly’ in our city motto. Thank
  you for your time.

  Wendy Warren – I have lived in El Monte for over 50 years. I support Irma Zamorano to
  be appointed to the City Council she would do a great job for the people of El Monte.

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Discussion and Action Regarding Council Communications.

  Previously the Council passed a motion to limit Council Communications of each
  Council Member to five minutes. I wanted to remove that limitation because I
  think as elected members of the City of El Monte we should not be limited to the
  amount of time we are able to speak. There has often been times when our
  meetings we run out of time and we have gone up to two months without being
  able to speak about our Council communications. When we do have the
  opportunity to speak I don’t think that we should be limited.

  11
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 5, 2021

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Martinez Muela  4-0
  To remove the 5 minute time limitation

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  18B.1 Update Regarding the Citywide Broadbantsd Accessibility.

  I wanted to reiterate that working in collaboration with staff as I mentioned in the
  past this pandemic has definitely demonstrated where structurally where we as a
  community have some places where we can improve and that would be the
  broadband accessibility. With respect to assuring that our community particularly
  our students who are experiencing distance learning one more semester that
  they have some degree of connectivity.

  18B.2 Update Regarding Citywide Street Repairs and the Three (3) Year CIP
  Progress Report.

  We have been going through some infrastructure development throughout the
  City particular on our streets some of the areas out on the Mountain View area
  have been finalized and I have heard from the community nothing but positive
  comments with respect to the work. Moving forward others are wondering when
  the repairs to your streets are coming.

  18B.3 Update Regarding the Park Master Plan, Maclaren Park and Lambert
  Park-Phase 1.

  I have been part of the conversations in regards of Maclaren Park with
  Supervisor Hilda Solis these efforts and create green spaces. I know that
  Lambert Park is going through Phase 1 so we are really happy that we are
  moving forward on this. Staff is working on grants to continue to move the Park
  Master Plan forward.

  18B.4 Update Regarding Crime Stats and Special Training from the El Monte
  Police Department.

  Our young community leaders are asking Council that we be open minded with
  respect to their concerns around policing. I know that our chief has been very
  proactive and very progressive in his contact in regards to training. Our youth
  community is looking forward to us being more progressive.

18C.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela
